Fosaprepitant, a neurokinin 1 (NK1) antagonist, is linked to Tacr1 through a well-documented binding interaction. The evidence suggests that Fosaprepitant, as part of the neurokinin 1 antagonist class, binds to Tacr1, which is a key receptor involved in the pathophysiology of nausea and vomiting. This mechanism is supported by the presence of Aprepitant, another member of the same class, which also binds to Tacr1 and is associated with antiemetic effects. The shared lowest common ancestor, Fosaprepitant and Aprepitant, further reinforces the classification and functional relationship between these entities.

The evidence also indicates that Fosaprepitant may contribute to the development of infusion site thrombophlebitis, a side effect that is mediated by Aprepitant. This suggests that the same receptor, Tacr1, may be involved in both the therapeutic effects and potential adverse effects of Fosaprepitant. The integration of these findings highlights the importance of Tacr1 in the pharmacological profile of Fosaprepitant, with the potential for further investigation into its role in both therapeutic and adverse outcomes.
